rationale_overall: This week's pool is thin on genuine investable catalysts. Filtered out as noise: private-company space news (SpaceX Falcon 9 launch, Starlink outage, T-Mobile satellite rollout — SpaceX is not investable), foreign-government items (Iran's Nahid-2 satellite launch, India/Pakistan missile tests, Australia missile trials — no US-listed tickers), a vague quantum-computing local-news piece with no company named, generic AI listicle clickbait ('this AI stock could join the $2 trillion club', 'second-half comeback' pieces from fool.com/biztoc with no verifiable new catalyst), a routine ABB customer order (Yueyang Paper) that isn't a wave inflection, and a Boeing labor dispute (contract rejection) that is negative/non-thematic rather than a buildup signal. The one borderline investable name — Globalstar (GSAT) expanding a ground station for its C-3 satellite system — is a real US-listed rockets/spacecraft-adjacent ticker, but the catalyst is incremental infrastructure news, not a strong enough inflection to justify swapping out any of the five current core AI/market holdings (AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA, SPY). No nuclear-restart ticker was identifiable (Michigan plant restart traces to privately-held Holtec, not a public equity). Absent a clearly stronger rising-wave vehicle, the watchlist is left unchanged this week.
